newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Christmas brings cheer to Nigerian naira.
newsitem.headline: Christmas brings cheer to Nigerian naira.

text.p: Nigeria's naira currency has risen sharply in value this month because of an injection of funds by Nigerians returning home for Christmas, money changers said on Monday.
"It is a seasonal development but nevertheless shows the power of market forces," said Salisu Umar, a leader of money changers on Broad Street, the Lagos equivalent of Wall Street.
"We have lots of dollars and pounds sterling which nobody seems to want and the rate is crashing fast," he added.
The naira was exchanging on the street on Monday at 67 to $1 compared with its autonomous foreign exchange market (AFEM) rate of 80 naira to the U.S. currency.
On AFEM, where the government auctions foreign exchange weekly, fewer banks have come forward to bid in the last two weeks, bankers said.
"The attraction of forex seems a little less now because industry is waiting for the budget to see what the policy for next year will be before returning to the market," said Fola Folusho, a banker.
Economists expect little change in the fiscal and monetary policy next year.

Under the policy of guided deregulation in place since last year, a few government transactions including debt servicing are undertaken at an official exchange rate of 22 naira to the dollar. All other businesses are conducted on the AFEM rate.
This has stabilised the naira rate at around 80 to the dollar for most of the year.
What the World Bank and Nigerian economists expect is the scrapping of the official rate next year to allow the market rate to rule throughout the system.
Money changers said they expected the naira to fall back to within its AFEM rate after Christmas.
"If you don't need (to buy) the naira now the best thing is to wait until mid-January to change because by then the holiday makers will have gone back," said Umar.
Many Nigerians resident abroad usually troop home for Christmas. British Airways, which flies to Lagos daily, says it is fully booked for the next several weeks.
